The hardest job on the farm just got easier

Prairie Post: Every day, technology makes life on the farm easier or more efficient. Now, grain cart operators are reaping the benefits.

Kevin Schulz,Editor,The FarmerOctober 30, 2026

link

Ten years after the last time I ran a grain cart, I once again had the opportunity to do what my dad always called the hardest job during harvest.

Maybe he said that because I made it look hard.

Just as technology has made a lot of jobs easier on the farm, there have also been advancements in the grain cart world.

I recently had the opportunity to attend a stop on the Fendt Harvest Tour at Phillips Farm near Hartland, Minn., where Fendt was showcasing its Ideal 8T combine with a 12-row Geringhoff cornhead eating through the acres. Phillips Farm was one stop during the 11-day tour that started in Ohio and ended in North Dakota on Oct. 22.

Of course, the Ideal 8T needed a catcher to hold what it pitched out from its hopper. A Fendt 1052 Vario tractor pulling a Haulmaster 1300 grain cart from Elmer’s Manufacturing was the perfect receiver. But what made it even more perfect is that both the tractor and the combine were equipped with the PTx OutRun.

Related:Surprising ways AI may improve your farm

This retrofit autonomy kit from Trimble allows pretty much hands-off operation. In this case, the grain cart was set to run by itself, under direction of the combine operator.

An iPad in the combine cab allows the person harvesting the crop to control the grain cart’s operation. With a touch of the iPad, the combine driver summons the tractor and grain cart to unload on the go. Parameters are predetermined for proper distance between the combine and cart, as well as the machines’ speed to prevent grain spillage.

It’s business as usual during harvest at Phillips Farm near Hartland, Minn., except for the fact that there is no driver in the tractor that is pulling the grain cart. (Kevin Schulz)

As mentioned above, it is pretty much hands off. While the tractor and grain cart can be directed into the truck loading zone, they cannot unload the grain into the waiting truck.

Some may argue that autonomy such as this replaces a human, but as we all know, finding good help has become the hardest job on the farm. A farmer can continue running the combine while the truck driver hauling the grain from the field to the grain setup can jump in the tractor to dump the grain cart into truck.

Sitting in the buddy seat (the main seat must be left vacant for autonomy to work) provided a surreal experience. I’m not used to sitting there letting someone else drive, especially when there is no one in the captain’s seat.

A lot of technology is cool simply for the “coolness factor,” but as a veteran grain cart driver, I could see the benefit of this advancement. This autonomy tech can also be used for tillage and planting operations or retrofitted to other equipment brands regardless of color.

Watch the video to ride along, just as I did, with “Otto,” as I labeled the autonomous driver.

About the Author

Kevin Schulz

Editor, The Farmer

Kevin Schulz joined The Farmer as editor in January of 2023, after spending two years as senior staff writer for Dakota Farmer and Nebraska Farmer magazines. Prior to joining these two magazines, he spent six years in a similar capacity with National Hog Farmer. Prior to joining National Hog Farmer, Schulz spent a long career as the editor of The Land magazine, an agricultural-rural life publication based in Mankato, Minn.

During his tenure at The Land, the publication grew from covering 55 Minnesota counties to encompassing the entire state, as well as 30 counties in northern Iowa. Covering all facets of Minnesota and Iowa agriculture, Schulz was able to stay close to his roots as a southern Minnesota farm boy raised on a corn, soybean and hog finishing farm.

One particular area where he stayed close to his roots is working with the FFA organization.

Covering the FFA programs stayed near and dear to his heart, and he has been recognized for such coverage over the years. He has received the Minnesota FFA Communicator of the Year award, was honored with the Minnesota Honorary FFA Degree in 2014 and inducted into the Minnesota FFA Hall of Fame in 2018.

Schulz attended South Dakota State University, majoring in agricultural journalism. He was also a member of Alpha Gamma Rho fraternity and now belongs to its alumni organization.

His family continues to live on a southern Minnesota farm near where he grew up. He and his wife, Carol, have raised two daughters: Kristi, a 2014 University of Minnesota graduate who is married to Eric Van Otterloo and teaches at Mankato (Minn.) East High School, and Haley, a 2018 graduate of University of Wisconsin-River Falls. She is married to John Peake and teaches in Hayward, Wis.

When not covering the agriculture industry on behalf of The Farmer's readers, Schulz enjoys spending time traveling with family, making it a quest to reach all 50 states — 47 so far — and three countries. He also enjoys reading, music, photography, playing basketball and enjoying nature and campfires with friends and family.

translationZh:
每天，科技都在让农场生活更轻松或更高效。如今，谷物车操作员也从中受益。

距离我上次驾驶谷物车已经过去十年，我再次有机会去做我父亲一直称之为收获季最辛苦的那项工作。

也许他这么说是因为我把它做得看起来很费劲。

正如科技让农场上的许多工作变得更轻松一样，谷物车领域也取得了进步。

最近我有机会参加了在明尼苏达州哈特兰附近菲利普斯农场举办的芬特收获之旅的一站活动，芬特在那里展示了其Ideal 8T联合收割机搭配12行格林霍夫玉米割台，高效收割大片农田。菲利普斯农场是这场为期11天之旅的其中一站，该旅程从俄亥俄州开始，于10月22日在北达科他州结束。

当然，Ideal 8T需要一辆接粮车来承接其粮仓卸出的谷物。一辆芬特1052 Vario拖拉机牵引着Elmer's Manufacturing公司的Haulmaster 1300谷物车，是完美的接收者。但更完美的是，拖拉机和联合收割机都配备了PTx OutRun。

这款来自Trimble的后装自动驾驶套件几乎可以实现完全无人操作。在本例中，谷物车被设置为在联合收割机操作员的指挥下自行运行。

联合收割机驾驶室内的iPad允许收割人员控制谷物车的运行。收割机驾驶员只需轻触iPad，即可召唤拖拉机和谷物车在行进中卸粮。联合收割机与谷物车之间的适当距离以及机器速度等参数均已预先设定，以防止谷物洒落。

在明尼苏达州哈特兰附近的菲利普斯农场，收获季一切照常，只是牵引谷物车的拖拉机里没有驾驶员。（Kevin Schulz）

如上所述，这几乎是完全无人操作的。虽然拖拉机和谷物车可以被引导至卡车装载区，但它们无法将谷物卸入等待的卡车中。

有人可能会认为这样的自动驾驶技术取代了人力，但众所周知，找到好帮手已成为农场最困难的工作。农民可以继续操作联合收割机，而将谷物从田间运往粮仓的卡车司机则可以跳上拖拉机，将谷物车中的谷物卸入卡车。

坐在副驾驶座上（主驾驶座必须空着，自动驾驶才能工作）是一种超现实的体验。我不习惯坐在那里让别人驾驶，尤其是当主驾驶座上没有人的时候。

很多科技仅仅因为“酷”而酷，但作为一名资深谷物车驾驶员，我能看到这项进步的好处。这项自动驾驶技术也可用于耕作和播种作业，或改装到其他品牌的设备上，无论设备颜色如何。

观看视频，与我一起乘坐——就像我一样——体验我称之为“Otto”的自动驾驶驾驶员。
